payload.title: A write command never appends text that cites a node id this store does not hold, without the operator being told

why: #240: hyp request-verify appended a why citing R-<new> with exit 0 in investigations/containment (commit 97219b1)

payload.title: Which rule stops a write command from appending text that cites an id that is no node?

why: #240's event: a why citing R-<new> was appended with exit 0

payload.title: Scan text flags for id-shaped tokens; warn on an unresolved one and still append
payload.body: Every write command scans --why, --body, --observation, --summary and each --limit for id-shaped tokens: at a word boundary, G-, Q-, H-, E- or R- (upper case) then six Crockford-base32 upper-case characters, or a placeholder mark (<, {, …, ..., or three or more X). Lower-case prose like E-mail is never id-shaped. A token not preceded by <name>: that does not resolve in this store prints warn: <flag> names <token>, which is no node here, and the event is still appended, exit 0.

why: #240 rival: tells the operator without blocking

payload.title: Scan text flags for id-shaped tokens; refuse an unresolved one
payload.body: Every write command scans --why, --body, --observation, --summary and each --limit for id-shaped tokens: at a word boundary, G-, Q-, H-, E- or R- (upper case) then six Crockford-base32 upper-case characters, or a placeholder mark (<, {, …, ..., or three or more X). Lower-case prose like E-mail is never id-shaped. A token not preceded by <name>: that does not resolve in this store refuses: nothing is appended and hyp exits 2, as for unknown node.

why: #240 rival: keeps the log free of unresolved cites

payload.title: request-verify, select and confirm take --result REF, resolved or refused
payload.body: request-verify, select and confirm take a repeatable --result REF. hyp resolves each ref to a Result in this store, or refuses with nothing appended and exit 2, and stores the ids in the event payload as results. Free text is not scanned.

why: #240 rival: makes the cited claim checkable instead of scanning prose

payload.title: No change: today's hyp is enough
payload.body: Today's hyp, unchanged, already tells the operator or refuses when a write command cites an id that is no node.

payload.title: Each rule's arm on the frozen fixture: exit, append and warning per case
payload.body: Zero tolerance. h-text-warn supports if its arm exits 0, appends and warns on every slip K1-K6, and exits 0, appends, no warn on every guard G1-G5. h-text-refuse supports if its arm exits non-zero, appends nothing on every slip, and exits 0, appends, no warn on every guard. h-cite supports if its arm refuses C1a and C1b with nothing appended, accepts C1c, and its G1-G5 rows equal today's. h-null contradicts if today appends any slip with exit 0 and no warn. Else contradicts (h-null: supports). Exit 3 after one re-run: inconclusive. Two or more supports: owner trade-off.

payload.observation: id-citation-arms@1 cases on the frozen fixture: the today arm appended every slip K1-K6 (K1 is the rebuilt event) with exit 0 and no warning. text-warn exited 0, appended and warned on K1-K6; text-refuse exited 2 and appended nothing on K1-K6; both gave exit 0, appended, no warning on G1-G5. cite refused C1a and C1b (exit 2, nothing appended), accepted C1c, and matched today on G1-G5. K7 (prose) passed every arm unflagged, unscored. verdict printed supports for three rivals: an owner trade-off.
limits: The fixture is hand-made apart from K1, and small: one store, and request-verify for most cases.
K7 is unscored for the scan arms: a scan cannot see an id that is not written.
The arms are prototypes; the delivered rule must be reproduced in Go and give the selected arm's rows on every case.
h-cite's cases run request-verify only; select and confirm take --result in the arm but no case runs them. Under h-cite the why still holds R-<new> (C1a).
The arm binaries are read from absolute paths outside the bundle, which the known-answer gate cannot see.

why: e-arms' pre-registered rule (8e5bc68), read from id-citation-arms@1 verdict
Owner chose h-text-refuse over h-text-warn and h-cite after kongming's counsel: R-BV4CWV supports all three; only refuse keeps the slip out of the log. Check stays write-time, exit 2.

payload.summary: Q-DVZZHY answered: h-text-refuse (H-88ZF3E) selected as the owner's trade-off on R-BV4CWV, verifier and owner sufficient.
